notes:
The 1,678 records that carry no `524$a`, read whole. Issue #220 asked what they are; the answer is that "no citation field" is not a collection but a symptom, and the records behind it are six digital series in `982$a`, five of which are not photograph catalogues at all.

958 are **newspaper issues** — San Francisco Bay Times (854, including its Coming Up! years), The Spokesman (54) and Hunter's Point Beacon (50). One record per issue: the title is the paper's name and the date, and the `856$u` files are per-page TIFF scans. A catalogue record for an issue cannot state a street number, and none does. Whatever addresses these papers carry are inside the page images, which is an OCR corpus and a different source, not this batch.

384 are **Sanborn atlas page images** — the six volumes of the 1899-1905 San Francisco insurance maps, one record per plate, titled `(Vol. 4, Page 467-468. San Francisco Sanborn Insurance Maps.)`. The addresses are drawn on the maps, not written in the catalogue.

331 are the **San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (PUC) Digital Collection** — Water Department photographs of the Hetch Hetchy system and the peninsula reservoirs. It is a genuine photograph collection, and it is the only one of the six, but its subject is mostly outside the city: Hetch Hetchy railroad construction, Groveland, Priest Tunnel, Moccasin, Crystal Springs, Sunol, Calaveras. Where a record is in San Francisco it locates itself by intersection — "Howard & 20th Sts.", "Market Street, opposite Spear Street", "47th Avenue South of Balboa St." — which is a block, not an address.

5 are Book Arts & Special Collections Center items (the Roxburghe Club's Anecdota SCOWAH).

Across all 1,678 records: **zero `650$a Streets--` headings, zero `500$a` address notes, zero assessor-block notes.** The catalogue states no address for any of them, in any field.

**The 37 records the issue counted as addressed are all false positives**, and they fall into two shapes:

- **23 Sanborn front matter pages** — covers, linings, title pages and index maps — whose title prints the atlas imprint: "Published by Sanborn-Perris Map Co. Limited, 115 Broadway, New York." Every one yields *115 Broadway*, which is the publisher's own New York office. This is the advertiser trap in AGENTS.md arriving through a title rather than a frequency count. EAS has no 115 Broadway, so these would have stayed unresolved rather than becoming wrong pages — but the two Broadway numbers either side of it, 100 and 120, are one live Financial District parcel.
- **14 PUC captions** where the number is a measurement or a sequence number: "1/4 Mile Below Big Oak", "1 Mile West of Big Creek Station", "Face of Priest Tunnel, 500 Ft. In", "Lantern Slide No. 55 A", "2 Miners in Tunnel", "BDPL 3 Section of 72\" Pipe", "Pulgas Outlet Tunnel + 1 Pulgas Temple".

No finding was written, because no record in the batch states a street number. The batch is closed.
